description: Quad buffer as LED data level shifter
notes: SOIC-14. 5V rail TTL thresholds so 3.3V reads high. ONE GATE USED, THREE SPARE (ADR 0016 - one strip); tie every spare input. The WS2815 datasheet's own recommended application circuit GROUNDS the first pixel's BI (L1 pin 6 to pin 5), so only DI is driven. WS2815 THRESHOLD VERIFIED: V_IH = 0.7 x VDD in a table whose header declares VDD = 4.5-5.5V, so 3.15-3.85V, which this part clears at 5V. Do not read that VDD as the +12V LED rail

description: HF decoupling at every carrier IC - ADC, reference, buffer, level shifter, sensor
notes: One per supply pin: MCP3202, REF5050 IN AND OUT, OPA2197 +12V, 74AHCT125, MPXV4006DP, and both R-78E5 inputs. ADR 0001 fixed only the shift registers (C-DECOUPLE-165) and stopped there | 2026-09-21: QTY 7 -> 8. The old enumeration gave the REF5050 one 100nF while carrier.md drew one at its OUTPUT and the prose claimed one at the sensor's VS pin - the same part spent twice across three files, and none drawn at VS at all. SBOS410O section 9.4.1.1 pp.29-30 wants both: a VIN bypass AND 'a high-frequency, 1uF capacitor in parallel between the output and ground'. Settled allocation is REF5050 VIN, REF5050 VOUT, and U-BREATH VS (pin 2) - and the VS one is the 100 nF the reference buffer's compensation is designed against. See figures.yaml cref-out-node

description: Series resistor on the WS2815 data line at the driver
notes: Damps the fastest edge in the instrument at its source and protects the 74AHCT125 output. ONE: one strip (ADR 0016). BI is NOT driven - the datasheet (datasheets/led/WS2815.pdf) grounds the first pixel's BI (L1 pin 6 to pin 5), so it needs no gate and no resistor. The figure is a raster with no text layer and was read by rendering at 700dpi - confirm visually before wiring

description: Pull-down on the LED data line at the MCU pin
notes: IO1 is high-impedance through the bootloader window, and a floating WS2815 data line is the classic source of intermittent LED behaviour. WHAT DECIDES IT: E1, where the strip first runs - if the boot window shows no spurious pixels without it, it is not needed. One part, one strip (ADR 0016)

package: 4 plated holes, drill 1.0 (THT pads, no part)
notes: Four conductors: DI through R-LED-SER, BI, and strip power. *** BI IS A GROUND CONNECTION, NOT A DRIVEN ONE *** - see the page; wiring it as a second data line is the mistake these pads invite. The +12V and GND pads carry strip power but that net belongs to carrier/power-entry-instrument, not to this circuit. PADS, NOT A CONNECTOR: the strip lies on the same board (ADR 0016), so its leads solder straight in. A plug would add 7-10 mm of height and a pigtail loop [ds JST-XH-SERIES.pdf p.1] to guard against a reversal that, with pads, can only happen once - at the build. SILKSCREEN EACH PAD 12V / DI / BI / GND, SQUARE PAD ON GND, AND CHECK 12V-TO-GND WITH A METER BEFORE FIRST POWER: reversed, 12V goes into the gate driver's output. Replacing the strip means desoldering four leads
